You are a hardware-debug reviewer. A first debug agent diagnosed an RISC-V RTL failure and an explain.png diagram was drawn from that diagnosis (explain.png sha256 first 16 hex: aea9b3822fdfd6e6).

Failing trace window (same window the first diagnosis saw):
- tb_picosoc_uart seed 42
- divider 64 loopback send 0xa5
tohost: FAIL 0xdead
TRAP: uart data mismatch got 0xff want 0xa5
CYCLES=2652
- /home/tuncay/afterglow/sim/tb/picosoc-uart-div_tb.sv:86: Verilog $finish
- S i m u l a t i o n   R e p o r t: Verilator 5.052 2026-09-05
- Verilator: $finish at 27ns; walltime 0.001 s; speed 42.930 us/s
- Verilator: cpu 0.001 s on 1 threads; allocated 4 MB
First diagnosis (verbatim):
ser_tx stayed idle so loopback RX got 0xff vs want 0xa5, causing TRAP: uart data mismatch got 0xff want 0xa5 and tohost FAIL 0xdead. Root cause is picosoc/simpleuart.v:130 `send_divcnt > (cfg_divider >> 4)` which makes the TX bit period 16x too short for divider 64, so the receiver samples idle and returns 0xff. Control wiring per picosoc/picosoc.v:197 reg_div_we and picosoc/picosoc.v:201 reg_dat_we confirms the divider-configured TX path; trace wins over sparse CONE_SLICE.
First patch_diff:
diff --git a/picosoc/simpleuart.v b/picosoc/simpleuart.v
--- a/picosoc/simpleuart.v
+++ b/picosoc/simpleuart.v
@@ -127,7 +127,7 @@
 				send_bitcnt <= 10;
 				send_divcnt <= 0;
 			end else
-			if (send_divcnt > (cfg_divider >> 4) && send_bitcnt) begin
+			if (send_divcnt > cfg_divider && send_bitcnt) begin
 				send_pattern <= {1'b1, send_pattern[9:1]};
 				send_bitcnt <= send_bitcnt - 1;
 				send_divcnt <= 0;
Look at the diagram (explain.png in the run bundle) together with the trace above. Either CONFIRM the first diagnosis (it explains the failing signal and the diff fixes it) or REVISE it (it misnames the signal or the diff is wrong). Reply JSON ONLY with keys: decision (exactly "CONFIRM" or "REVISE"), diagnosis (final diagnosis text), patch_diff (final unified diff), reason (one sentence: why the diagram confirms or what it corrects).
